page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. This configuration provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES. Memory capacity stands at 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates that the r5n.4xlarge delivers average multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. In stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests, the instance scores in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests, including both cached small-block and uncached large-block reads, also register in the average category, with uncached read speeds reaching 87.18 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5n.4xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. The instance is suited for workloads such as Redis in-memory databases, where it achieves an average benchmark of 13.18 million SET operations per second, as well as static web serving and medium-scale database operations. It is less suited for compute-heavy single-threaded tasks or large-scale language model inference.
